items.title: Decide whether to pay the disputed €498.00 'invoice'
items.action: Before paying anything, verify whether you actually requested or want this private land register listing; this letter itself says it is only an offer and no contract exists until you pay, so you are not obligated to pay it.

warnings: This letter is styled as a 'Rechnung' (invoice) but its own small print says it is merely an offer (Angebot) that only becomes a binding contract once you pay — a tactic used in known scam/misleading-invoice schemes.

The document itself states the listing is in a private register unrelated to the official German land register (Grundbuch), so paying it does not give you any official land registration and may be money paid for an unwanted or unnecessary private directory entry.
Consider not paying and, if unsure, checking with consumer protection (Verbraucherzentrale) or reporting the sender before transferring any money.
data.title: Disputed "invoice" for a private land register entry (Grundstücksregister Online Service GmbH)
data.summary: Grundstücksregister Online Service GmbH sent an invoice-style letter dated 19 November 2026 demanding €498.00 by 1 December 2026 for a 2-year "entry" of the property Ackerstraße 26 in a private register, explicitly stating this register is unrelated to the official German land register (Grundbuch) and that the letter is only an offer, not yet a contract.
data.explanation: This looks like a misleading commercial offer rather than an official bill: the small print admits it is only an "Angebot" (offer) and that a contract only arises if you pay, and that the listing has nothing to do with the official Grundbuch. You are not legally required to pay it. Before doing anything, check whether you ever requested such a listing; if not, it is safer to ignore or report it rather than pay. If you are unsure, consumer protection services (Verbraucherzentrale) can confirm whether this is a known scam pattern. Do not pay simply because of the stated deadline.
